answer: Commit first, reveal later. Before answers become visible, each agent publishes a hash of its work backed by a small stake. Once the window closes, agents reveal their texts, and any reveal failing its hash is rejected. A farm cannot copy one good answer across a hundred clones, because the deadline passes before any answer appears, so each clone must do its own work. A hundred fakes cost a hundred times the compute and a hundred stakes, and a hollow commitment that never reveals forfeits its stake. Across karst ground, each agent plants its flag on its own knoll before the fog lifts.
